newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-March 27.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-March 27.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Thursday morning:
** India's stockmarket watchdog on Wednesday pledged to set up a committee to review the carry-forward system of share trading, currently allowed only under strict conditions.

Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) chairman D.R. Mehta also said the regulator had decided on a uniform lock-in period of three years for promoters' contributions to equity. Currently, the lock-in period varies from two to five years.

** India's Finance Ministry and central bank on Wednesday signed an agreement which would discipline fiscal spending by forcing the government to raise funds for its temporary cash needs at market interest rates.

Reserve Bank of India (RBI) governor Chakravarti Rangarajan and Finance Secretary Montek Singh Ahluwalia signed the agreement to introduce a new system of central bank funding to meet the government's borrowing needs in 1997/98 (April-March).
** ABB plans to give a thrust to its instrumentation business in India and make it a source point for the international market, the Observer paper says.

The paper quoted the managing director of ABB Control Valves as saying the main reason for the shift in focus on India was because the Asia Pacific region was growing faster than the traditional markets or western Europe ane the United States.
** The Indian rupee opened at 35.91/93 against the dollar on Thursday compared to the previous close of 35.88/89, dealers said.
Dollar selling pressure is seen continuing on Thursday. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is seen as the only significant dollar buyer in the market, dealers said.
** Shares at major Indian exchanges ended mostly lower on Wednesday and brokers termed the market weakness a speculator sell-off amid little buying activity by foreign funds.
The benchmark 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange index .BSESN lost 32.54 points to 3,733.24.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index .NSEI was up 0.85 points to 1,059.20.
** The Delhi share index .DE lost 1.38 points to 783.23.
** The Calcutta share index .CALSN slipped 2.87 points to 454.28.
** The Madras share index .MDSI dropped 33.42 points to 3,567.69.
